what_it_does: FPGAs (field-programmable gate arrays) are chips whose internal circuitry can be reconfigured in software to act as a custom hardware accelerator for a specific task. Cloud providers rent out FPGAs to customers, but different generations or models of FPGA from different vendors differ in their internal wiring and control interfaces, making it very hard to write an accelerator that works on more than one type. Harmonia is a framework that defines a standard "contract" between the FPGA's platform-specific management layer and the customer's custom logic, so the customer can write their accelerator once and deploy it on any supported FPGA model. It also provides a software layer that hides the per-FPGA differences from user programs, so the same application code runs unchanged across a heterogeneous fleet of FPGAs.
